thesis_statement: T-Mobile is the scaled US wireless share-taker converting best-network differentiation into industry-leading financial growth: postpaid service revenue +13%, Core Adjusted EBITDA +12%, record NPS of 46, with UScellular integration absorbing one-time costs while the 5G capacity lead and new-business lines (broadband, fiber JVs) extend the runway.

base.summary: Postpaid ARPA (+2%) and account growth keep service revenue growing high-single to low-double digits, EBITDA margin holds, and UScellular merger costs fade from the comparisons.
drivers: Adjusted Free Cash Flow $4.8B +4% despite merger costs

bull.summary: Best-network lead compounds (record NPS 46, third consecutive Ookla Best Network award), broadband and fiber JVs scale into a second growth leg, and ARPA acceleration returns post-integration.
drivers: record wireless NPS 46 (highest ever for a big-three carrier)

bear.summary: Postpaid net account additions decelerate (-13% YoY this quarter) as the market saturates and cable/competition intensifies; ARPA growth slows below 1% and the growth premium de-rates toward utility.
drivers: UScellular integration costs ($146M net accelerated depreciation in the quarter)
market saturation with intensifying price competition

key_risks: Account growth is decelerating: postpaid net account additions fell 13% YoY; ARPA growth (+2%) must carry more of the revenue algorithm.
UScellular merger integration adds costs and execution risk (accelerated depreciation $146M net in Q2; EPS growth of 5% was held below service-revenue growth by these costs).
Net debt ~$116.6B is the structural feature of the wireless business model; rate sensitivity of that debt stack is a macro risk.
Saturation: with three national carriers plus cable MVNOs, the industry growth pool is mature; the thesis is share and ARPA, not market expansion.
